name: Turkesterone

lead: Turkesterone is a phytoecdysteroid, a plant steroid structurally related to insect molting hormones, first isolated from Ajuga turkestanica. It became popular in supplements as a purported natural anabolic.

Claims rest largely on rodent studies and on research into the better-known ecdysterone. Human trials of turkesterone specifically are small and mostly have not shown meaningful muscle or strength benefits; the wiki's rating is limited.

paras: In animals, ecdysteroids appear to increase muscle protein synthesis, possibly via estrogen receptor beta and signalling pathways, rather than through the androgen receptor. How well turkesterone is absorbed and whether these findings apply to people are unresolved.

It is sold as a dietary supplement in the US, with unresolved novel-food status in the EU. Short-term human studies have not reported serious harm, but long-term data are lacking, and independent testing has found products containing far less turkesterone than labelled.
